heroText: Rabat is Morocco's coastal capital, a calmer counterpart to Marrakech and Fes with royal palaces set among wide boulevards and gardens. First-time visitors should climb the unfinished Hassan Tower beside its mausoleum, wander the blue-and-white lanes of the Kasbah of the Udayas, and explore the Roman and Merinid ruins at Chellah. Rabat-Sale Airport sits just across the river, making the capital an easy, low-key base.

areas.name: Kasbah of the Udayas
areas.text: The Kasbah of the Udayas is a fortified blue-and-white quarter overlooking the river mouth, with narrow lanes, a museum and Andalusian gardens.

areas.name: Medina
areas.text: Rabat's Medina is smaller and calmer than Fes or Marrakech, with souks, guesthouses and easy access to the train station.

areas.name: Agdal
areas.text: Agdal is a modern residential and business district with shops, cafes and government offices, popular with longer-stay visitors.

areas.name: Hassan
areas.text: Hassan is the central district around the Hassan Tower and its mausoleum, walkable to the Medina and train station.

airports.name: Rabat-Sale Airport (RBA)
airports.text: Rabat-Sale Airport lies just north of the city across the Bou Regreg river, a short taxi ride from central Rabat hotels.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Rabat-Sale Airport (RBA) and central Rabat before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Stay in the Medina or Hassan district for walkable access to the Kasbah of the Udayas, Hassan Tower and the train station, or choose Agdal for a quieter, more residential base with modern cafes and shops. Rabat's compact size makes most areas easy to combine.
hotelIntro: Rabat's Medina and Hassan district hold guesthouses and mid-range hotels close to the main sights, while Agdal offers newer business hotels suited to longer stays or government-related visits.
rentalCars: A rental car is useful for day trips along the coast or to nearby Meknes, but unnecessary for getting around compact central Rabat.

travelTips.title: Combine with Sale
travelTips.text: Cross the Bou Regreg river by tram or boat to the sister city of Sale for a quieter medina and fewer crowds.

travelTips.title: Visit Chellah for the storks
travelTips.text: Time a Chellah visit for late afternoon to see storks nesting on the ruined minaret alongside the Merinid tombs.

travelTips.title: Dress respectfully at the mausoleum
travelTips.text: Dress modestly when visiting the Mohammed V Mausoleum, an active royal site with guards in traditional dress.

travelTips.title: Use the tram
travelTips.text: Rabat's tram line is an easy, inexpensive way to move between the Medina, Agdal and Sale without needing a taxi.

history.text: In 1150 or 1151 the Almohad caliph Abd al-Mu'min built a new kasbah (citadel) to replace the former ribat, within which he included a palace and a mosque.

history.label: 15th century
history.text: During the Marinid dynasty period (13th to 15th centuries), the town of Salé across the river grew more important than the settlements of the south bank.
In 1515 Leo Africanus reported that Rabat had declined so much that only 100 inhabited houses remained.
